papers.title_in_file: Optimal Stratification of a Sampling Frame: A Comparative Study of Classical, Quantum, and Quantum-Inspired Approaches
papers.version_note: arXiv:2608.10787v1 [stat.ME], 11 Aug 2026; the text is the paper its record names.
papers.what_it_is: A case study that runs one 20-stratum survey-stratification QUBO surrogate on a simulated-annealing stand-in for D-Wave, IBM QAOA, QCi Dirac-3 and a GPU Ising machine, and compares each with a classical genetic algorithm that optimises the Bethel sample size directly.

existing.note: The numbers are right. Section 6.1 limits the reading of 'genuine optimisation': the authors say the device's native energy scale is not documented well enough to certify from it alone that the search was effective, as opposed to merely well-behaved. The 100-variable free-tier cap is stated in Section 5.1, and the 160 and 129 figures are the best-known results, not certified optima.
existing.value: The authors report that on the twenty-stratum frame, under the free-tier cap of one hundred decision variables, the QCi Dirac-3 partition has a Bethel sample size of 286, against 160 for the best-known QUBO solution (Fixstars Amplify AE, a GPU Ising machine) and 129 for the SamplingStrata genetic algorithm; re-evaluated under the common one-hot objective its energy is 936.61 against the best-known 501.0. The authors say the Dirac-3 run shows evidence of a non-trivial optimisation process, but that its native energy scale is not documented well enough to certify from it alone that the underlying search was effective.

existing.reader_inference: The 286 against 160 comparison isolates the device, because 160 is already the surrogate's best-known Bethel value; the 160 against 129 part is the formulation's share. The paper does not compare the Dirac-3 run to a random baseline, as it does for IBM.

assertions.value: The authors report that 10,000 uniformly random four-cluster assignments of the same twenty atomic strata, evaluated with the same Bethel-Chromy allocator, have sample sizes with a median of 314 and a range from 162 to 383, and that IBM's value lies at approximately the 12th percentile of that distribution. assertions.value: The authors state that an initially considered Dirac-3 qudit formulation with squared label differences was inappropriate for nominal cluster labels, because it introduces an artificial ordering and, with non-negative weights, is minimised by giving every atomic stratum the same label; the study therefore uses the one-hot QUBO.

is minimised by assigning every atomic stratum the same label, the degenerate single-cluster solution

assertions.value: The authors define the surrogate as a population-weighted pairwise within-cluster dispersion: plain Euclidean distance between standardised mean and standard-deviation feature vectors, scaled by the square root of the product of the two strata's populations. They state this is a design choice and that its relationship to the squared-distance pairwise identity is heuristic, not derived.

the relationship between them is heuristic rather than derived

so CB(z) has no direct QUBO representation

papers.what_it_is: A numerical proposal that designs, by invariant-based inverse engineering of a shortcut to adiabaticity, a control field for a single-qubit quantum perceptron so that its excitation probability gives a sigmoid activation function in a shorter operation time than the FAQUAD protocol.

existing.note: The abstract claims faster performance and enhanced robustness against imperfections in the controls. The body supports the speed claim with minimum operation times (0.2 for the cubic ansatz and 0.15 for the fifth-order ansatz against 0.3 for FAQUAD). The only robustness result in the body is robustness to variations in the operation time t f (timing errors); insensitivity to the kappa parameter is also shown. No other control imperfection (amplitude noise, detuning, decoherence) is simulated.
existing.value: The authors propose a quantum perceptron in which a control field is inversely engineered, giving a rapid nonlinear response with a sigmoid activation function, and report faster overall performance than quasi-adiabatic protocols; the robustness shown in the body is to timing errors, that is, variations on the operation time t f.

However, for the approximate Helstrom measurement scheme, the number of copies does not depend on the dimension of the states at all, so it can be more eﬃcient for high-dimensional states.
This eﬃciency comes at the price of having to manipulate all copies coherently.
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation with a stated assumption that each unitary has the same error, not a formal theorem.
assertions.reader_inference: The text compares this with tomography cost O(d2/ǫ) here, which differs from the O(d2/ǫ2) of Section 4.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that exploiting the analytic solution of the representer-theorem strategy is expected to reach the same accuracy with fewer copies of the two states than the generic bound.
quotes: Therefore, exploiting the analytic solution (75) is expected to provide an advantage to get the same accuracy with fewer copies of the two states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Compares two upper bounds for pure states; the authors write expected.

assertions.value: The authors state that the scaling with the number of test copies V is worse for a transductive process than for an inductive one, by an amount that depends on how the single-copy error depends on S.
quotes: The scaling with V will therefore be worse than for an inductive process – how much worse depends on how the single-copy error depends on S.
assertions.certainty_reason: Argued by splitting the training set among V test states.

assertions.value: The authors state that if V is at most polynomial in n and ǫ is independent of n, the transductive strategy may provide an exponential advantage in n over tomography-based methods, while in the big data regime where V is large the inductive strategy may be preferable.
quotes: if V is at most polynomial in n and ǫ is independent on n, the transductive strategy may provide an exponential (in n) advantage compared with tomography based methods.
On the other hand, in the “big data” regime, where V is large, the inductive strategy may be preferable.
assertions.certainty_reason: Compares the two upper bounds of the displayed comparison; hedged with may.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is between upper bounds for specific protocols, not a proved separation.

assertions.value: The authors state that their Rademacher complexity bound proves the conjecture of reference 8 that the generalization error only slightly increases with the number of copies used in the majority vote, while the training error decreases exponentially in V.
assertions.anchor: Section 5.1.1, p.39; Appendix B part 3, p.53
quotes: thus providing a proof of the conjecture from [8], namely that the generalization error only slightly increases with the number of copies used in the majority vote.
Since the training error decreases exponentially with V , using more shots is expected to be beneﬁcial, as long as we have enough data to make (104) small.
assertions.certainty_reason: A proof is given in Appendix B part 3 but the bound formula is garbled in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that with S going to infinity only the generalization error remains, with a single copy per state only the knowledge gap remains, and that for large finite S both appear.
quotes: so that the only source of error is the generalization error (with no excess testing error or knowledge gap)
We have no generalization error, since the average states ρ¯+ and ρ¯− are precisely what we want to discriminate between, and so the only source of error is the knowledge gap.
assertions.certainty_reason: Argued in prose for the two extremes.

assertions.value: The authors state that for tomography-based classification increasing S decreases only the knowledge gap, increasing N decreases both errors, and for large d the knowledge gap dominates.
quotes: Thus, increasing S decreases only the knowledge gap, whilst increasing N decreases both the knowledge gap and the generalization error. For large d, the knowledge gap will dominate.
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from the tomography knowledge-gap scaling and the Rademacher bound.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the approximate Helstrom measurement via state exponentiation, if neither the knowledge gap nor the generalization error is to dominate for large N, S must also be increased.
quotes: Thus, if we do not want either the knowledge gap or the generalization error to dominate (for large enough N ), we must also increase S.
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from combining the two error scalings of the section.

assertions.value: The authors state that for imperfect copies produced by a slow environment, if V is of order S the dependence on S and V disappears from the generalization error, at the price of a different mutual information that includes the environment.
quotes: Therefore, if V = O(S) the dependence on either S and V disappears from the generalization error, making it independent on the number of copies employed either during training or testing.
However, the price to pay is modeled by a diﬀerent mutual information
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from the displayed bound, whose formula is garbled in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that for observables with bounded 2-norm the generalization bound does not explicitly depend on properties of the quantum state, and that for Pauli-sum observables the bound grows exponentially with the number of qubits unless the coefficients are rescaled by an exponentially small quantity.
quotes: For observables with bounded 2-norm, generalization does not explicitly depend on the properties of the quantum state.
Therefore, unless the coeﬃcients αj are rescaled with an exponentially small quantity, the bound (113) grows exponentially with the number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived in Appendix B part 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that for observables with maximum eigenvalue equal to 1 the generalization bound is equivalent to that for optimizing over POVMs, and for the hinge loss the bounds are exactly equal.
quotes: For observables with maximum eigenvalue equal to 1, we can focus on G∞ with c∞ = 1
For the hinge loss, where λ = 1, the bounds are exactly equal.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived in Appendix B part 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that classifying a new state with the kernel expansion requires evaluating new kernels, which consumes further copies of the training states, so the strategy is transductive.
quotes: Notice that for prediction the evaluation of new kernels k(xn, x) is necessary, which requires further copies of the training states ρ(xn), as discussed in Section 1.
This strategy is therefore transductive.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5.5 states the setup of the strategy.

assertions.value: The authors state that the error with S copies scales as O(S to the minus 1/2) with a prefactor that diverges when the two average states are close, so less distinguishable states need more shots.
quotes: In this way, we can use Eq. (95) to show that the error using S copies scales as O(S−1/2), but with a prefactor that diverges when ρS+ ≃ ρ¯S−.
Accordingly, if the states are less distinguishable more shots are required.
assertions.certainty_reason: A lower bound from Jensen's inequality, not a full analysis of the kernel loss.

assertions.value: The authors state that both the Caro et al and Du et al bounds show that PQCs with many trainable gates incur a larger generalization error on a fixed number of examples, and that the Du et al bound suggests gate noise may not hurt generalization.
quotes: both bounds show that PQCs with large number of trainable gates, Ng, incur a larger generalization error when trained on a ﬁxed set of N examples
may not be detrimental to generalization and can help prevent over-ﬁtting

assertions.value: The authors state that the Rademacher bounds of Caro et al and Du et al, which scale with the number of trainable parameters, cannot explain the low generalization error of QNNs observed in the over-parameterized regime, and that an encoding-based bound can help.

assertions.value: The authors state that characterizing the excess risk of quantum generative models that approximate an unknown quantum state from S copies is an open problem, and that generalization analysis of quantum generative models has been studied in very few works.

the generalization analysis of quantum generative models has been studied in very few existing works

However, since the Helstrom classiﬁer uses unconstrained operations, it is unlikely to be optimal for generalization.

papers.version_note: arXiv:2405.06580v1, 10 May 2024. The text layer holds the paper once. Parts of Section 2 are printed one word per line, and the figure bodies (circuit diagrams, plots) carry no text beyond captions and axis labels.
papers.what_it_is: A proposal and simulation study of a continuous-variable quantum Boltzmann machine that prepares a thermal state with a CV quantum imaginary time evolution circuit and is trained to generate continuous probability distributions from SAR image histograms, standard distributions and CV quantum states.

existing.note: The paper names one device, the Xanadu X-series cloud chip, and the reason (no online squeezers). The stored value says 'the available hardware' without naming the device. The same passage also says the currently available photonic devices have limitations that prevent a realization on cloud-accessed on-chip hardware.
existing.value: The authors state that the Xanadu X-series, a cloud-accessed photonic quantum chip, cannot accommodate their CVQBM, mainly because of the lack of online squeezers, since the parameters of the available offline squeezers are fixed.
quotes: the Xanadu X-series [33], which is a cloud-accessed quantum chip that includes squeezers, beam splitters, and interferometers cannot accommodate our CVQBM mainly due to the lack of online squeezers (the parameters of the available offline squeezers are fixed)

No further action is taken on the hidden mode.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Embeddings for Many Body Quantum Systems
papers.version_note: arXiv:2309.08666v2 (19 Jun 2024); the record id says 2024 and the file name says 2023 (the v1 year).
papers.what_it_is: A variational scheme that embeds an accurate active-space model, classical or a quantum circuit, in a cheaper bath model, tested on Ising chains and ammonia with simulated quantum circuits.

existing.note: The two quotes are in different places: the first is in the Abstract only and the second in the Discussion only. The quantum parts of every run are on classical simulators without noise, so the tests are not on quantum hardware.
existing.value: The authors state they demonstrate the protocol on spin chains and small molecules and have successfully tested the method on spin systems and molecular Hamiltonians; the quantum hardware contribution is evaluated on a classical simulator.
existing.anchor: Abstract; Discussion, p.5; Molecular system, p.4
quotes: We demonstrate the effectiveness of the protocol on spin chains and small molecules and provide insights into its accuracy and computational cost.
We have successfully tested our method on spin systems and molecular Hamiltonians, demonstrating its potential.
The quantum hardware contribution is evaluated on a classical simulator.
existing.certainty_reason: An author claim of effectiveness, and an empirical result from one study.

existing.value: The authors state that, from the quantum computation perspective, the effect of hardware noise on the results should be investigated.
quotes: Under the quantum computation perspective, the effect of hardware noise on the results should be investigated.
existing.certainty_reason: The Discussion states the limit; the Fig. 2 caption and Appendices C and F confirm the runs are noiseless simulations.

quotes: The variational ansatz Ψθ,δ(σ, η) is therefore obtained as the product of the two different ansatzes αθ(σ|η) βδ(η) depending on a set of parameters {θ, δ}.

quotes: The proposed method is completely variational and global, meaning that the parameters of both models are optimized simultaneously.

assertions.value: The authors state that the sum over active configurations scales exponentially in the number of active degrees of freedom, so it can be performed only if the active partition is small enough, and that avoiding sampling of the active partition is preferred where Markov Chain Monte Carlo suffers critical slowing down.

assertions.value: The authors state that every step of the procedure can be accomplished efficiently in polynomial time with respect to the system size.
assertions.anchor: Embedding quantum devices, end of section

assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this assumption and its meaning in Appendix A.
